records.title: Introduction and Manual Scope
records.summary: How to use this manual, confidence ratings, safety and revision control.
records.text: Purpose. How to use this manual, confidence ratings, safety and revision control. Overview This chapter forms part of the working technical record for the 2009 Knaus Sun Traveller. It explains the system in practical terms, identifies the checks an owner should carry out and separates confirmed information from items still awaiting an identification plate, wiring trace or manufacturer document. The correct approach is to inspect first, measure second and replace parts only after the fault or requirement has been confirmed. Photograph every connector before disconnecting it. Record fuse ratings, cable colours and component labels exactly as found on the vehicle. Key information Purpose and scope of the vehicle-specific reference Confidence labels for confirmed, probable and pending information Safety isolation before electrical, gas, water or mechanical work Revision history and ownership records Inspection procedure Make the system safe. Disconnect 230 V hook-up and isolate the relevant battery or gas supply where the task requires it. Carry out a visual inspection before moving any wiring, pipework or fittings. Look for heat, corrosion, abrasion, leaks, loose fasteners and previous modifications. Confirm the supply and control conditions required for normal operation. Use a digital multimeter for electrical checks and approved leak-detection methods for gas work. Compare findings with the photographs, fuse tables and service records stored in this app. After any repair, test the complete operating sequence and record the date, mileage, parts used and result in the Service Log. Owner checklist Identification label photographed and readable Connections and mounting inspected Correct supply or fluid level confirmed Safety devices tested where applicable Findings entered in the service record Verification status Mixed verification. Vehicle-specific observations are separated from general service guidance. Important. Do not use generic torque figures, fuse uprating or unverified connector pinouts. The app marks model-specific gaps so they remain visible rather than being filled with assumptions. Official Knaus reference Foreword and use of the manufacturer documentation This manufacturer manual is the MJ 2006 edition supplied directly by Knaus. Use it as the official Sun-Traveller model-family reference, then match every option and component to your 2009 vehicle. Open official manual at PDF page 9

records.title: POWER SUPPLY 11.6.2 Charger
records.summary: POWER SUPPLY 11.6.2 Charger The use of high-quality electronics means that the charger operates virtually without loss of power. The automatic charging process charges the batteries gently and without harmful overloading, thereby considerab
records.text: POWER SUPPLY 11.6.2 Charger The use of high-quality electronics means that the charger operates virtually without loss of power. The automatic charging process charges the batteries gently and without harmful overloading, thereby considerably enhancing battery life. The charger has outputs for the starter battery (Battery 1) and the backup battery (Battery 2). The charger starts to operate as soon as it is connected to the 230 V supply. The auxiliary battery can be charged outside the mobile home using the charger through the KNAUS adapter cable which is available as an extra option: 씰 Remove the auxiliary battery through the service flap, unplug the charger under the seating module and take out of the mount. 씰 Use the adapter cable to charge the auxiliary battery in an appropriate room by connecting the charger to a 230 Volt outlet. You will find further information about the battery charger in the separate operating instructions from the manufacturer. 11.6.3 Example Showing How to Calculate Electricity Consumption (using 95 Ah battery) These values are „approximate figures“ and depend on the related model. records.text: FOREWORD 1. FOREWORD We wish you all the best for your KNAUS mobile home. Your „holiday home on wheels“ has been designed and manufactured to give you the maximum possible enjoyment. Please read through this manual carefully before using the vehicle to ensure you get the very best out of your mobile home. Take the time to be able to enjoy the excellent comfort and high technical standards of your mobile home in a manner that is as relaxed as possible. Please pay particular attention to the safety information. In addition to this manual you should also familiarise yourself with the separate manual for the base vehicle and the appliances fitted. If your mobile home is fitted with optional equipment, observe the accompanying special permits and the related special instructions. To request maintenance and repair work and if you have any special questions, please call your nearest KNAUS dealer. The staff at your authorised dealership will be happy to advise and assist you on all matters relating to your WEINSBERG product. Only approved spare parts from the original manufacturer can ensure quality and a perfect fit. We cannot fulfil our warranty obligations according to the terms of our warranty if maintenance work has been neglected or carried out incorrectly. Please send your completed warranty card to KNAUS TABBERT GROUP GMBH to activate the warranty. This manual is only valid in so far as the mobile home corresponds to the specifications described within. The mobile home specifications are particularly important when making enquiries and ordering spare parts. Model name: Type designation: Therefore please make a note of the model, type, Year of manufacture: year of manufacture and the chassis number of your KNAUS caravan on this tablet. Chassis number: You will find these details on the rating plate. This is located in front under the bonnet on the FIAT chassis and on the passenger side on the inside frame on the RENAULT chassis. We wish you plenty of leisure time enjoyment with your new KNAUS mobile home. The Management SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 1-1

Open the gas bottle stop valve and gas tap for the heater „ ”. 3. Place rotary knob (item 1, page 12-1) at the required thermostat setting 1-9, green indicator (3) illuminates and indicates the position for the room temperature set. 4. Set rotary switch (2) to the operating position (5). Further information on the operation of the heater can be found in the separate manual from the manufacturer. CAUTION: Work on the electronic control unit for the Trumatic may only be carried out by a qualified and trained service engineer.  If the green indicator (3) does not light up, replace the fuse in the electronic control unit or the fuse for the battery monitor.  The yellow indicator lamp (8) lights up while the hot water boiler is heating up.  A continuously lit red indicator lamp (9) indicates a closed gas bottle shut-off valve and/or device shut-off valve, interrupted air-flow, air in the gas line or a faulty fuse. The fault is reset by turning the appliance off and then on again.  If the red indicator (9) flashes, the operating voltage supplied to the appliance is too low (recharge battery). You will find further information in the separate manual supplied by the manufacturer. 12.1.3 Adjusting the Heater/Boiler 씰 Turn the rotary knob (item 1, page 12-1) to the desired room temperature - the integral thermostat will now automatically maintain a constant temperature to your setting. records.text: HEATING & HOT WATER As all other appliances in the water circuit (water pump, taps etc.) are not protected by the frost protection valve and the automatic drain could be obstructed by dirt or ice, the water must be drained after the boiler is turned off if there is a risk of frost. You will find further information on draining the hot water boiler in the separate manual supplied by the manufacturer. 12.2 Hot water central heating The hot water central heating including the integrated hot water heating system is located under the seating module and is controlled with the adjacent control element. The heater can also be operated with the hot water boiler drained. The heater (radiators) that are fed with a circulating pump with glycol fluid are distributed so that an even temperature is achieved throughout the interior of the mobile home. When using the central heating in the mobile home, you do not have to do without the enjoyment of a comfortable indoor temperature - similar to a living room. The heater in the rear of the mobile home can also be included or excluded from the heating circuit. This allows you to set an individual room temperature for the sleeping area. In heating operation, the heater automatically switches the circulating pump on according to the temperature difference between the set room temperature and the actual room temperature. When the desired temperature is achieved, the circulating pump switches off automatically. records.title: HEATING & HOT WATER CAUTION:
records.summary: HEATING & HOT WATER CAUTION: Work on the electronic control unit for the heating may only be carried out by a qualified and trained service engineer. The heating has an ionising flame control, i.e. if the flame goes out, the electronic cont
records.text: HEATING & HOT WATER CAUTION: Work on the electronic control unit for the heating may only be carried out by a qualified and trained service engineer. The heating has an ionising flame control, i.e. if the flame goes out, the electronic control unit attempts to light it again. If the flame does not ignite within 10 seconds again, the solenoid shuts the gas feed off and blocks the electronic control unit. This procedure is indicated by the red LED illuminating (Item G, page 12-6). If the room thermostat starts heating operation, i.e. if the temperature in the mobile home is under the set temperature, the circulating pump is started. This starts the fluid in the heating system to circulate and cold fluid enters the heating circuit. The operating thermostat for the heating registers the fluid temperature and the heating system warms the fluid that circulates through the system. If the set temperature is achieved, the circulating pump is switched off. The operating thermostat registers that the fluid has achieved the set temperature and the heating unit is switched off. As soon as the fluid temperature has dropped a few degrees, the heating unit is switched on again. This ensures that heated fluid is always running through the heating circuit if the thermostat is operating the heating. 12.2.2 Heating comfort In order to best utilise the principle of water-based heat, it is important that the heated air can circulate under the bed boxes and behind the back cushions freely. It is just as important that the cushions and covers do not hinder the air circulation behind the back cushions. To achieve an individual room temperature in the rear sleeping area of the mobile home, a „bypass switch“ enables the heating radiator to be included or excluded from the circulation system as desired. In affected models, this is done with a shut-off valve in the clothes closet that switches the heating radiator on or off depending on the setting: Control horizontal (in direction of line) = radiator off Control vertical (across line direction) = radiator on SUN-TRAVELLER 12-8 MJ 2006 • 10.2005 SPORT-TRAVELLER

records.summary: HEATING & HOT WATER 12.2.3 Circulating pump CAUTION: Continuous operation will decrease the service life of the circulating pump! Switch the circulating pump off if it is not requried. In the expansion tank, there is a 12 V operated circula
records.text: HEATING & HOT WATER 12.2.3 Circulating pump CAUTION: Continuous operation will decrease the service life of the circulating pump! Switch the circulating pump off if it is not requried. In the expansion tank, there is a 12 V operated circulating pump that circulates teh heated glycol fluid in the heating system. The circulating pump starts by actuating the slider switch on the controller (page 12-6) in setting „I“ or „J“. Afterwards, the room thermostat regulates the on and off switching for the circulation pump depending on heating requirements. 12.2.4 Expansion tank The level of the glycol fluid can be monitored in the expansion tank. This should be at approx. 1 cm over the „MIN“ mark when the heating unit is cold (see figure below). The heating circuit is to be filled with a 40% glycol mix as is used in automobile engines. If the heating system is subjected to temperature under -25 °C, the glycol mixture is to be increased, but never to above 50%. Before filling with new fluid, check the actual glycol content so that the glycol concentration in the fluid mixture is not increased too much. The glycol mixture should be changed every 2 years since important characteristics such as e.g. corrosion protection can deteriorate over time. The heating system is never to be allowed to sit without glycol fluid. If the fluid level in the expansion tank drops lower than normal condensation, the entire heating system must be checked for leaks. If glycol fluid is leaking, the affected spot is to be rinsed thoroughly with water and then dried. To fill the glycol mixture, proceed as follows: 1 WARNING: Be careful when filling the glycol mixture. Fluid is poisonous! 1. Unscrew the cap nut (1) on the expansion tank and lift the circulating pump. 2. Slowly pour the glycol mixture into the expansion tank until it reaches a level approximately 1 cm over the „MIN“ mark. Hot water central heating: Expansion tank SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 12-9

records.summary: HEATING & HOT WATER CAUTION: After filling the glycol mixture, you must bleed the air from the heating unit before starting again! 12.2.5 Bleeding the air from the heating system Depending on the circulatory system installed, air pockets ca
records.text: HEATING & HOT WATER CAUTION: After filling the glycol mixture, you must bleed the air from the heating unit before starting again! 12.2.5 Bleeding the air from the heating system Depending on the circulatory system installed, air pockets can be created during filling. You will notice that when there is air in the heating system the heat only reaches about 1 m down the line although the circulating pump is running. If the heating system has just been filled, small air bubbles can be created in the expansion tank. If the circulating pump is shut off for a few seconds, the air bubbles will disappear under normal circumstances. An effective method of bleeding and filling the heating system is to use a filling pump from ALDE (optional extra). To bleed the air from the heating system, proceed as follows: 1. Switch the heating unit on, move the slider switch (page 12-6) to position „B“ – „C“ – „D“ or „F“. 2. Ensure that the circulating pump is switched off and set the slider switch (page 12-6) to position „H“. 3. Open the bleed screws for all radiators one after the other and leave them open until fluid runs out. 4. Now switch the circulating pump back on, move the slider switch (page 12-6) to position „I“ or „J“ and let it run for a few minutes. Check for whether the lines and the radiators are warm everywhere. 5. If these measures do not have the desired effect you may have to fill with glycol again. Otherwise continue as follows: CAUTION: The mobile home is not to be raised using the support legs! 1. Park the mobile home on a slope or raise it with an appropriate jack so that it leans forward. Secure the mobile home against rolling! 2. Wait several minutes with the mobile home in this position so that the air in the heating system can rise to the top. 3. Unscrew the bleed screw at the highest point (should be determined earlier) and wait until fluid comes out. 4. Park the mobile home on a slope or raise it with an appropriate jack so that it leans backward. Secure the mobile home against rolling! Repeat the previously executed procedures. SUN-TRAVELLER 12-10 MJ 2006 • 10.2005 SPORT-TRAVELLER

The hot water boiler can be operated with liquid gas, with 230 V (electric cartridge) or with both simultaneously. The 9 litre hot water boiler provides hot water within a temperature range of 40 to 70 °C. At maximum usage, approximately 17 litres of hot water at a temperature of 40°C is possible. The hot water boiler requires approx. 30 minutes to heat 12 litres of water from 5°C to 40°C when working with liquid gas. An operating pressure of about 1.8 bar builds up in the water pump when the main switch is turned on. This ensures that pressure is available when water is required. Should the pressure fall below a certain limit while water is being drawn (pressure drop) the nominal pressure of 1.8 bar is automatically restored. records.summary: COOKING & BAKING 13. COOKING & BACKING 13.1 Using the Gas Cooker 1. Open gas bottle shut-off valve and „ ” gas shut-off valve on the valve block under the kitchen range. 2. Lift up the cover on the hob. WARNING:  To ensure a continuous flo
records.text: COOKING & BAKING 13. COOKING & BACKING 13.1 Using the Gas Cooker 1. Open gas bottle shut-off valve and „ ” gas shut-off valve on the valve block under the kitchen range. 2. Lift up the cover on the hob. WARNING:  To ensure a continuous flow of air in the mobile home, the forced air vents in the roof, mushroom vents and in the entry must never be covered!  When using the cooker you must open a window or roof light to ensure an adequate supply of oxygen to the interior of your mobi- le home!  The gas cooker should never be used as a heater!  Explosion hazard - Never allow gas to escape unburned!  The user must be able to keep the gas lighting process in full view - this must not be concealed by pots etc!  The flame safety cover must be lifted up whenever the cooker is in use! 3. Turn the controller for the desired burner counter clockwise to small or large flame, press and hold. 4. Light the escaping gas with suitable lighter and keep the control knob held down for another 5 to 7 seconds. The flame may go out if the control knob is released too soon. Repeat the operation if this happens. 5. To switch off, turn the control knob clockwise to the „  ” position. 6. If the thermocouple is bent or faulty the burner will not operate correctly and the flame will keep going out even though the control knob is pressed for a longer time again and again. If this happens a new thermocouple must be fitted by a qualified engineer. NOTE: A flame with an indistinct pattern is a sign of poor combustion, and we therefore recommend annual servicing by a qualified engineer. You will find further information in the separate operating instructions supplied by the cooker manufacturer. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 13-1

records.summary: TOILET 16. TOILET 16.1 Thetford Unit CAUTION: The Thetford unit should only be drained on sites with suitable sewage systems or specially designated disposal facilities! 1. Before using the toilet, push down the flush button briefly to allo
records.text: TOILET 16. TOILET 16.1 Thetford Unit CAUTION: The Thetford unit should only be drained on sites with suitable sewage systems or specially designated disposal facilities! 1. Before using the toilet, push down the flush button briefly to allow a small amount of water into the bowl. Repeat as necessary. The flow of water stops when the button is released. 2. After use, push down the flush button and turn counter-clockwise at the same time. This turning motion opens the valve in the WC. The toilet bowl is flushed thoroughly but is economical on water. 3. After flushing, turn the flush button clockwise to close the valve again. The toilet can also be used with the valve open. CAUTION:  If there is a risk of frost and the mobile home is not heated the Thetford unit should be drained to prevent it from freezing.  In winter the toilet flush should not be used until the toilet cubicle has thoroughly warmed up otherwise the water pump in the Thetford flush may be damaged.  An environmentally friendly and fully bio-degradable chemical WC additive should be used for the WC.  If environmental concerns exist, the WC can also be used without chemical additives but the Thetford unit will require more fre- quent draining as a result. You will find further information on the Thetford toilet in the separate manual supplied by the manufacturer. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 16-1

records.text: WINTER CAMPING 17. WINTER CAMPING 17.1 General Notes on Winter Camping If you plan to enjoy the freedom of camping life in winter as much as in summer, then here are some hints which you should follow:  After driving on roads that have been sprayed with salt, wash the underbody of the base vehicle with water.  Find out as much as you can about weather and driving conditions before you set out and during your journey.  Your mobile home has all-round insulation and double glazing and is perfectly ‘winter-worthy’ if used correctly. The water supply is inside the vehicle on all models.  Proper ventilation is just as important in winter as it is in summer. Ski boots and other wet items will increase the level of moisture and condensation inside the mobile home.  Heating is of course particularly important in winter, For this reason the heating – the heaters installed as standard are normally adequate – is particularly important for winter camping. Quick removal of the water vapour generated by cooking, wet clothing and breathing is particularly important for camping in winter. In addition to good ventilation, the heated air will rapidly eliminate the water vapour, as warm air can absorb much more moisture than cold air. When there is moisture in the air, the lower the room temperature the quicker that condensation will form if there is a slight difference between the temperature of the room air and the temperature on the inside wall.  The windows, window frames and the corners of storage lockers are particularly prone to condensation depending on use, the number of persons, the site and the level of humidity both inside and outside the mobile home. Adequate heating of the mobile home with the recirculation fan switched on will improve this situation. 17.2 Additional Notes on Winter Camping  Secure the mobile home against rolling away then release the parking brake to prevent it from freezing.  Place all cushions in the mobile home upright to ensure that they are aired and dried.  Use only 100 % propane in winter as butane will not gasify below freezing point. Make sure you have an adequate supply of gas bottles.  Avoid the use of electrical appliances that consume a lot of power. Campsites do not have unlimited amounts of electricity.  In cold weather the water pipes in the mobile home can freeze if the vehicle is left for long periods with the heating switched off.  To prevent freezing, drain the wastewater tank with the heating off, please refer to Section 10.5.  The backup battery (battery 2) should be kept fully charged at all times.  While heating up the vehicle, open all cupboards, flaps and storage lockers to prevent condensation forming. electricity.  in cold weather the water pipes in the mobile home can freeze if the vehicle is left for long periods with the heating switched off.  to prevent freezing, drain the wastewater tank with the heating off, please refer to section 10.5.  the backup battery (battery 2) should be kept fully charged at all times.  while heating up the vehicle, open all cupboards, flaps and storage lockers to prevent condensation forming. sun-traveller sport-traveller mj 2006 • 10.2005 17-1

records.text: WINTER CAMPING  Avoid storing containers (bottles, cans etc.) with water, juice or other liquids in the unheated mobile home as they may freeze.  All snow and ice should be carefully removed from the roof of the vehicle and from the awning; it is particularly important to ensure that the flue on the side wall is kept free at all times.  Always keep the forced air vents open, and open the roof light slightly if required.  Never run power cables on the ground - they may freeze to the soil or be damaged by snow clearing vehicles.  Keep metal taps open in an unheated mobile home at low temperatures, even if the water system has been drained. Always remember to open the mixer lever in both the cold water (blue) and the hot water (red) positions and then to leave it in one of these opened positions. 17.3 Recommended Accessories for Winter Camping To be prepared for any eventuality when winter camping, we recommend the following accessories: Comments: Date: ❄ Winter cover for the refrigerator (optional extra) OK: ❑ ❄ Snow shovel OK: ❑ ❄ Brush OK: ❑ ❄ Plastic ice scraper OK: ❑ ❄ Deicer spray OK: ❑ ❄ Talcum powder or Vaseline OK: ❑ ❄ Cooking salt or environmentally friendly anti-freeze additive for the wastewater tank OK: ❑ ❄ Snow slip mats OK: ❑ ❄ Snow chains (Caution: Snow chains are not permitted for use with alloy wheels) OK: ❑ ❄ Jump starting cables OK: ❑ ❄ A bag of sand is always useful should you get stuck in snow OK: ❑ ❄ OK: ❑ For your own notes ❄ OK: ❑ ❄ OK: ❑ ❄ OK: ❑ Copy if necessary SUN-TRAVELLER 17-2 MJ 2006 • 10.2005 SPORT-TRAVELLER

records.summary: CLEANING & CARE 19. CLEANING & CARE 19.1 Cleaning and Care of the Exterior of the Mobile Home The outer skin of the mobile home is made from aluminium sheet. The surface of this aluminium sheet is stove enamelled with an acrylic paint. This
records.text: CLEANING & CARE 19. CLEANING & CARE 19.1 Cleaning and Care of the Exterior of the Mobile Home The outer skin of the mobile home is made from aluminium sheet. The surface of this aluminium sheet is stove enamelled with an acrylic paint. This process - known as polyester coil coating - is a modern, environmentally friendly way of surface finis- hing which creates high colour brilliance and is extremely durable. To maintain the high quality of the finish you should care for the paintwork as described below: 씰 Salt, soot, bird droppings and other aggressive substances should always be removed from the paintwork of the mobile home immediately before they have time to leave a stain. 씰 Wash your mobile home with water regularly if you are near the sea. You should clean your mobile home as you would a car: WARNING: Take extra caution when walking over the roof of the vehicle when wet or icy. There is an increased danger of slipping or falling off! CAUTION: 墌 Avoid localised loads (e.g. kneeling) as far as possible if you need to go onto the roof of the mobile home! Walk only in the horizontal areas of the mobile home roof and wear soft-soled shoes (e.g. trainers or pumps)! 墌 Avoid walking on the mobile home roof with textured-soled footwear as any stones embedded in the soles will dent the outer skin of the mobile home! 씰 Shampoo your mobile home with a pH neutral product (pH: 6-8). Don’t forget the roof! 씰 Now thoroughly rinse off the vehicle with water, and dry. 씰 Use only sponges, soft cloths or soft brushes. Hard tools can damage the paintwork. 씰 The mobile home should be waxed from time to time to protect and enhance its sheen. Apply the coat of wax as directed by the manufacturer. 씰 To freshen up old paint, the mobile home can be treated with a suitable polish. Here again, you should follow the manufacturer’s directions. Polishing can attack the paint surface of your mobile home (abrasion) so do not apply polish unless absolutely necessary. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 19-1

records.summary: CLEANING & CARE 씰 Plastic parts must not be treated with aggressive cleaning agents (benzene, methylated spirits, thinners, etc.), on this topic see section 19.1.1. 씰 Tar stains or other organic stains on the painted surface are best remove
records.text: CLEANING & CARE 씰 Plastic parts must not be treated with aggressive cleaning agents (benzene, methylated spirits, thinners, etc.), on this topic see section 19.1.1. 씰 Tar stains or other organic stains on the painted surface are best removed with benzene. We strongly advise against the use of other solvents! Insects should be softened with water and then removed with a sponge wrapped in a nylon stocking. 씰 Damage to the surface of your mobile home should be repaired immediately with refinish paint to prevent corrosion taking a hold. 씰 Check the condition of the underbody protection once a year. Please contact your KNAUS dealer if the underbody protection is damaged. 씰 After driving on roads that have been sprayed with salt, wash the underbody of the base vehicle with water. 19.1.1 Cleaning Plastic Parts on the Exterior of the Mobile Home 씰 Plastic products can be carefully cleaned using warm water with the addition of a very slightly acidic, neutral or very slightly alkaline cleaner. 씰 You can use low concentrations (< 2 %) of mild household cleaners dissolved in water. 씰 Abrasive agents like scouring powder are not recommended as they will scratch plastic surfaces. 씰 Very greasy or oily surfaces can be washed down with petroleum substances free from aromatic compounds such as ethanol. records.text: MAINTENANCE & INSPECTION 20. MAINTENANCE & INSPECTION 20.1 Servicing For the sake of road safety your mobile home must be regularly and properly serviced, just like a car. CAUTION: 墌 Carrying out maintenance work on your mobile home requires specialist skills and knowledge. This is why you should have your mobile home serviced only by an authorised service centre. 墌 The service centre will stamp your Customer Service Record Book to confirm that the leak tests on all tanks and pipes, hoses etc. have been carried out. 墌 If any parts need replacing, ensure that the manufacturer’s original spare parts are used. NOTE: For mobile homes that are not used very often, servicing should be carried out once a year and in plenty of time before the start of a journey. 20.2 Intervals for Statutory Testing and Exhaust Gas Test Under Section 29 StVZO, mobile homes under 3.5 t registered in Germany must be tested every 2 years (by TÜV, DEKRA); mobile homes over 3.5 t must be tested annually. In Germany all vehicles must also undergo an exhaust gas test at the intervals shown in the table opposite. The test sticker on the Engine Cat Maximum Inspection front number plate will tell you when the next test is due (see also type total weight interval Section 23.1 Statutory tests). Turbo Diesel Yes Over 3.5 tonnes Annually Turbo Diesel Yes Up to 3.5 tonnes Every 2 Years NOTE: The relevant regulations which Petrol engine Yes – Every 2 Years apply in other countries must be complied with! records.summary: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 2.3 Safety Devices Particular attention should be paid to the safety devices fitted to your mobile home. These safety devices must be regularly checked to ensure that they are working correctly. The mobile home must not
records.text: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 2.3 Safety Devices Particular attention should be paid to the safety devices fitted to your mobile home. These safety devices must be regularly checked to ensure that they are working correctly. The mobile home must not be operated if the safety devices are malfunctioning or not working. SAFETY ALWAYS COMES FIRST! 2.4 Saftey regulations for participation in traffic  The mobile home must be officially registered.  The driver must have a respective driver’s license.  The mobile home is designed for a maximum speed of 120 km/h. A maximum speed of 130 km/h is shown in the vehicle registration document. In Germany the admissible top speed for mobile homes is: Urban areas: to 3,5 tonnes total weight .... 50 km/h over 3,5 tonnes total weight .... 50 km/h Outside urban areas: to 3,5 tonnes total weight .... 100 km/h over 3,5 tonnes total weight .... 80 km/h On motorways: to 3,5 tonnes total weight .... no speed limit over 3,5 tonnes total weight .... 80 km/h  In Germany , it is basically permitted to carry persons in the living area of the mobile home during the journey in accordance with StVZO. However these persons may only use the seats equipped with safety belts. Seats that are not equipped with safety belts are not to be used while travelling. Persons facing forward in the living area of the mobile home while the vehicle is in motion must wear the three-point seat belts. Those persons that are sitting opposite the direction of travel in the living area of the mobile home must also wear a safety belt. For journeys abroad the regulations in the specific country are to be observed! We recommend that the safety belt be worn at all times in moving vehicles.  Due to the vehicle height you need to be aware of the mobile home’s vulnerability to side winds during the journey.  Note the maximum total load (see vehicle certificate, no. 15) and maximum technically permissible axle loads (no. 16).  Distribute the payload evenly throughout the mobile home (see section 4.3ff Payload).  During the journey all seats must be turned to face the direction of travel and locked in place. records.summary: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS  Before beginning your journey, the support legs (accessories) are to be fold up and locked.  Before beginning the journey check for whether the entrance door, toilet door and bath door, the cabinet doors, drawers and
records.text: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS  Before beginning your journey, the support legs (accessories) are to be fold up and locked.  Before beginning the journey check for whether the entrance door, toilet door and bath door, the cabinet doors, drawers and flaps and all windows and roof lights are closed. The refrigerator door must be completely closed and blocked with the door latch.  If accessories are fitted this will alter the dimensions, the total weight and the handling of the mobile home. Such accessories may have to be entered in the vehicle documents.  When parking the mobile home, pull the parking brake on as far as it will go.  Use wheel chock if parking on a slope.  Keep the roof clear from ice and snow in the winter.  Never use snow chains on mobile homes fitted with aluminium wheels.  If the vehicle is transported (e.g. by train, lorry), the vehicle must be loaded in the direction of travel! 2.5 General Safety Instructions  Always ensure there is adequate ventilation when residing in the mobile home. Forced air vents in the roof lights must never be obstructed (e.g. by winter mats) or sealed because of the risk of suffocation from increased CO (carbon monoxide) levels in the air.  You must carry with you at all times, read and understand the individual manuals for all installed systems (e.g. gas heater, gas cooker, refrigerator etc.) and the base vehicle (engine, brakes etc.).  Note the headroom of the entry door and the heights of the driver and passenger doors.  Close all doors and windows when leaving the vehicle.  Take care not to damage the outer skin of the mobile home!  Avoid localised loads (e.g. kneeling) as far as possible if you need to go onto the roof of the mobile home!  Walk only in the horizontal areas of the mobile home roof and wear soft-soled shoes (e.g. trainers or pumps)! Avoid walking on the roof with textured-soled footwear as any stones embedded in the soles will dent the outer skin of the mobile home!  Take care when climbing onto a wet or icy mobile home roof. 2.5 general safety instructions  always ensure there is adequate ventilation when residing in the mobile home. forced air vents in the roof lights must never be obstructed (e.g. by winter mats) or sealed because of the risk of suffocation from increased co (carbon monoxide) levels in the air.  you must carry with you at all times, read and understand the individual manuals for all installed systems (e.g. gas heater, gas cooker, refrigerator etc.) and the base vehicle (engine, brakes etc.).  note the headroom of the entry door and the heights of the driver and passenger doors.  close all doors and windows when leaving the vehicle.  take care not to damage the outer skin of the mobile home!  avoid localised loads (e.g. kneeling) as far as possible if you need to go onto the roof of the mobile home!  walk only in the horizontal areas of the mobile home roof and wear soft-soled shoes (e.g. trainers or pumps)! avoid walking on the roof with textured-soled footwear as any stones embedded in the soles will dent the outer skin of the mobile home!  take care when climbing onto a wet or icy mobile home roof. there is a danger of slipping or falling off! records.summary: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 2.5.1 Safety regulations for version with rear carrier systems CAUTION: After fitting rear carrier system always note the following:  only carry items that are intended to be carried and are listed in the respective ope
records.text: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 2.5.1 Safety regulations for version with rear carrier systems CAUTION: After fitting rear carrier system always note the following:  only carry items that are intended to be carried and are listed in the respective operating manual of the rear carrier!  that the load is attached and secured to the rear carrier according to instructions!  the admissible payload capacity of the rear carrier is not exceeded!  that the axle load distribution and the total weight of the mobile home will be altered!  that the handling and braking of the mobile home will be altered!  Only have rear carrier systems fitted by authorised workshops for safety reasons! Your responsible KNAUS-dealer will be glad to inform you of an authorised workshop in your vicinity. 2.6 Towing and being towed CAUTION: To prevent severe damage to the chassis and body, the tow rope, cable or bar is to be mounted on the front on the intended eyelets for towing the mobile home! records.title: SPECIFICATIONS 22.2.2 Explanations on the Payload Calculation
records.summary: SPECIFICATIONS 22.2.2 Explanations on the Payload Calculation WARNING:  The permitted total weight of the mobile home specified in the vehicle documentation must not be exceeded!  An overloaded mobile home can go out of control while driv
records.text: SPECIFICATIONS 22.2.2 Explanations on the Payload Calculation WARNING:  The permitted total weight of the mobile home specified in the vehicle documentation must not be exceeded!  An overloaded mobile home can go out of control while driving!  Loading the mobile home is to be performed according to section 4.3.1!  We recommend that you have the fully loaded vehicle weighed on a public weighbridge before commencing your journey.  If the determined total weight of your mobile home has exceeded the permitted total weight, all guarantee claims to the manufacturer are voided and also insurance claims! The payload is the difference between the permitted total weight and empty weight EEC Directive 92/21/EEC governs the payload of mobile homes at European level. The regulations specified there closely correspond with standard DIN EN 1646-2. 22.2.2.1 Empty weight The mass of the vehicle in running order is the mass of the empty vehicle (including lubricants, toolkit, spare wheel, 90 % full fuel tank), with factory-fitted standard equipment, plus the weight of the driver (75 kg) and the basic equipment (see section 21.2.2.2). 22.2.2.2 Basic Equipment The basic equipment comprises all items of equipment and fluids that are necessary for the safe and proper use of the mobile home. It includes the weights of:  Gas: Liquid gas bottles (up to 90% full)  Water: Fresh water heater (100% full) Fresh water tank (90% full) SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 22-9

records.text: SPECIFICATIONS 22.2.2.3 Maximum total weight This weight allows for specific operating conditions including factors such as material strength, load capacity of the tyres etc. This weight must not be exceeded under any circumstances! NOTE: You will find the maximum technically permissible laden mass, the mass in running order and the payload in the specifications on pages 22-12 to 22-76. 22.2.3 Weights of the Payload 22.2.3.1 Weights of the Accessories The accessories cover the weights of all objects that are available beyond the standard equipment. records.title: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 2.7 Safety Instructions for the Gas System
records.summary: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 2.7 Safety Instructions for the Gas System WARNING: To avoid damage to persons and/or property, always ensure that any gas operated devices that are installed at a later point in time are equipped for an operating pressu
records.text: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 2.7 Safety Instructions for the Gas System WARNING: To avoid damage to persons and/or property, always ensure that any gas operated devices that are installed at a later point in time are equipped for an operating pressure of 30 Millibar [mbar].  Any installations or modifications to the gas system must be carried out by authorised specialists!  The LPG (liquefied petroleum gas) system is inspected by an engineer before it leaves the factory. The gas system must be re-inspected every 2 years and following any modifications and repairs.  To ensure a continuous flow of air in the caravan, the forced air vents in the roof, mushroom vents and in the entry must never be covered! WARNING: When operating the gas cooker, violation of the following information will result in an acute danger of death from oxygen starvation and the possible production of odourless and poisonous carbon monoxide (CO)!  When using the gas cooker you must open a roof light, a window or the doors!  The mobile home must never be heated with radiant heaters and other appliances that take their combustion air from the interior of the vehicle!  Before starting up the gas heater remove any dirt and snow from the flue and the combustion air inlets to prevent carbon monoxide (CO) in the exhaust gas increasing to an inadmissible level!  The gas locker must be hermetically sealed from the interior of the mobile home and there must be a ventilation opening on or immediately above the floor of at least 100 cm2, which must never be covered!  Gas bottles must be kept in the gas locker where they must be held upright and secured to prevent them from spinning round!  Do not store current-drawing devices (e.g. batteries) and/or devices which form a source of ignition in the gas locker!  Electrical leads may only be fed through the gas locker if insulated. Do not fasten with clips!  Only use pressure regulators with a safety valve! Other regulators are not permitted! Connect the regulator to the gas bottle carefully by hand (do not use spanners, pliers or similar). The threaded fittings on the gas regulator have left-hand threads. Use a de-icing system for the regulator for temperatures below 5 °C (e.g. Eis-Ex). SUN-TRAVELLER 2-6 MJ 2006 • 09.2005 SPORT-TRAVELLER

records.text: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS  When switching on gas appliances (e.g. gas cooker) which are ignited by pressing a button, it must be ensured that this automatically returns to its original position after pressing!  The exhaust gas pipe from the gas heater must be rising along its entire length and be fastened securely in place with clips and gas exhaust pipe supports if necessary!  The flue pipe must be properly connected and sealed to the gas heater and to the flue, and must not be damaged in any way.  Appliances which operate with gas must not be used while refuelling or in a garage!  Operate the gas system only with propane, butane or a mix of the two gas types! Propane can gasify down to -32 °C, butane only down to 0 °C.  The gas bottle stop valve must be closed while travelling if no appliances are in use!  Always close the appliance gas tap when you have finished using a gas appliance!  If the mobile home is not to be used for a long period, close the gas bottle stop valve on the gas bottle!  The regulators and flue pipes must also be checked regularly! Inspections must be recorded on the test certificate according to DVGW Worksheet G 607. The operator is solely responsible for ensuring the checks are carried out!  Observe relevant national legislation outside Germany! WARNING: If you smell gas or suspect a gas leak, proceed immediately as follows:  Close gas bottle stop valve!  Avoid ignition sources of any sort incl. naked flames or smoking!  Provide ventilation through the room!  Clear the danger area!  Inform the campsite superintendent and the fire service if necessary! NOTE: The gas system must be started again by a trained specialist after being checked. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 09.2005 2-7

records.title: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 2.8 Safety regulations for the electrical system
records.summary: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 2.8 Safety regulations for the electrical system 2.8.1 Starter and auxiliary battery WARNING: 墌 To prevent sparking and fire hazards, the negative cable of the starter or auxiliary battery is to be disconnected before th
records.text: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 2.8 Safety regulations for the electrical system 2.8.1 Starter and auxiliary battery WARNING: 墌 To prevent sparking and fire hazards, the negative cable of the starter or auxiliary battery is to be disconnected before the positive cable when removing. 墌 When installing the starter or auxiliary battery, the positive cable is connected first and then the negative cable. 墌 To avoid short-circuits and the fire hazards, only insulated battery clamps are to be used. Battery jumper cables must also be equipped with insulated battery clamps! 2.9 Fire Safety 2.9.1 Prevention of Fire Hazards 墌 All repairs and modifications to the electrical or LPG systems and equipment must be carried out by trained personnel! 墌 Never leave children unattended in the mobile home! 墌 Keep flammable materials away from heating and cooking appliances! 墌 Never use portable heating or cooking appliances! 2.9.2 Fire Fighting 墌 It is recommended to always carry a 1-kg dry powder fire extinguisher in the mobile home! This extinguisher must be approved, tested and kept within easy reach. 墌 The fire extinguisher must be checked regularly by approved trained personnel (make a note of the inspection date)! SUN-TRAVELLER 2-8 MJ 2006 • 09.2005 SPORT-TRAVELLER

records.text: SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS 2.9.3 In Case of Fire 墌 Evacuate all vehicle occupants! 墌 Switch off the electrical power supply and disconnect from the mains! 墌 Immediately close gas bottle stop valve! 墌 Sound the alarm and call the fire service! 墌 Try to put out the fire if this is possible without risk! 墌 Be aware of the location and use of emergency exits! 墌 Keep emergency exits clear! 墌 Follow the instructions for use of the fire extinguisher! 2.10 Important Notes for the Sanitary Area CAUTION: 墌 The wet cubicle is only allowed to be used for showering in conjunction with a shower curtain or a shower door! 墌 The toilet cubicle is only allowed to the cleaned with a damp cloth! 2.11 Environmental Notes 墌 Collect all operating fluids (e.g. lubricants, spent oil and detergents) in suitable containers and dispose of correctly! 墌 Never dispose of wastewater of any kind or domestic refuse in the gutter or in the countryside. 墌 Always empty the wastewater tank and the Thetford unit at disposal facilities on the campsite or at specially designated disposal facilities. Observe town and district regulations and ask about disposal facilities. 墌 Use an environmentally friendly and biologically degradable WC chemical in small doses. 墌 Separate domestic refuse into glass, metal tins, plastic and wet refuse. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 09.2005 2-9

records.summary: DESCRIPTION & EQUIPMENT 3. DESCRIPTION & EQUIPMENT 3.1 Chassis  A FIAT „Ducato“ or a RENAULT „Master“ chassis is used as the base vehicle for the KNAUS mobile home. You will find further information about the base vehicle in the separate o
records.text: DESCRIPTION & EQUIPMENT 3. DESCRIPTION & EQUIPMENT 3.1 Chassis  A FIAT „Ducato“ or a RENAULT „Master“ chassis is used as the base vehicle for the KNAUS mobile home. You will find further information about the base vehicle in the separate operating instructions by the respective company. 3.2 Superstructure  The mobile home is constructed in a „sandwich construction“ with a total thickness of up to 40 mm. The sandwich consists of a glued and compressed aluminium outer skin, polystyrene insulating material, wooden panelling and the interior wall. The gluing is a special feature of this type of construction. We use an adhesive which penetrates about 5 mm into both sides of the polystyrene, thereby cross-linking the material. The result is not just a surface join but also a homogenous bond between the components. Combined with precision workmanship, this process guarantees optimal thermal insulation.  The double-shell GFK roof of the mobile home is constructed in a single piece vacuum filled component. The GFK cover coat is applied with an additional surface coating (Gel coat) during manufacture.  The rear wall of the mobile home is also made of double-shell vacuum GFK contruction for wieght and stability optimisation.  Another feature of the KNAUS mobile home is the wooden panelling of the side walls, both in the contouring of the mobile home and in all essential recesses, windows and doors. This panelling lends the sidewalls a considerably increased stability.  The floor is constructed of so-called „multi-function flooring“ in the mobile home. This has an overall thickness of 60mm and is insulated with styrofoam. This insulation ensures that the floor is capable of withstanding Winter condions.  All of the equipment previously located in the interior of the mobile home and in the storage cabinets (besides the heating) are under the mobile home floor between the longitudinal beams of the vehicle chassis. This greatly increases the capacity of the storage cabinets in the mobile home since they are now located outside of the mobile home interior. 3.3 Gas locker  The separate, lockable gas locker is situated immediately behind the driver ’s door of the mobile home. The gas locker is insulated and hermetically sealed from the interior of the mobile home. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 3-1

records.title: DESCRIPTION & EQUIPMENT 3.4 Furniture
records.summary: DESCRIPTION & EQUIPMENT 3.4 Furniture  The furnishings are manufactured entirely from high quality materials. A very special technique is used to bend curved furniture. Furniture sections are made with multiple-bonded, upholstered wood. Th
records.text: DESCRIPTION & EQUIPMENT 3.4 Furniture  The furnishings are manufactured entirely from high quality materials. A very special technique is used to bend curved furniture. Furniture sections are made with multiple-bonded, upholstered wood. This type of finish ensures that furniture surfaces are simple and easy to keep clean. Certain items of furniture are also made using a combination of plywood and solid wood.  Particular attention is also paid to the securing of the furniture in the interior of all KNAUS mobile homes. To enable the absorption of correspondingly large forces, multi-laminated plywood strips are fastened to the sidewalls at certain places. Because these attachment points are incorporated during actual manufacture of the sidewalls they ensure a high level of strength.  All cupboard and locker doors are fitted with high-quality locks to prevent unwanted opening. All door fittings used in the mobile home have been chosen with great care. Here again, only the very best quality is used.  Depending on the model, the interior of the mobile home features a permanently installed rear bed and one or more seat modules which can be easily converted into sleeping berths. Spacious storage lockers are provided around the interior of the vehicle above the rear bed, the seating modules and the kitchen range. There are no storage lockers above the alcove bed. 3.5 Kitchen range  The kitchen range is fitted with a cooker, a sink and a refrigerator. The kitchen range also provides comprehensive surfaces and storage facilities.  There is lighting above the kitchen range in all models. Some models also have a pullout basket storage cabinet on castors to hold food and crockery. 3.6 Heater  The mobile home is either equipped with hot water central heating (ALDE) or with a powerful heater with warm air blower and warm water supply (TRUMA). Each mobile home also has an integral wet cubicle (toilet, bath and washroom). 3.7 Fresh water and waste water  All mobile homes have a built-in fresh water and wastewater tank. The fresh water and the waste water tanks in all Sun- Traveller models are insulated underneath with an insulating shell and is kept from freezing in cold weather with the warm air from the heater. Upon special request, the fresh water and the waste water tank can also be insulated and heated with a warm flow of air in all Sport-Traveller models. SUN-TRAVELLER 3-2 MJ 2006 • 10.2005 SPORT-TRAVELLER

records.text: BEFORE THE JOURNEY 4. BEFORE THE JOURNEY 4.1 Using the mobile home for the first time WARNING: Read all safety instructions thoroughly before using the mobile home! CAUTION:  The first time you use the mobile home, check the wheel bolts/wheel nuts are still tight after driving approx. 50 km and if necessary retighten. The correct tightening torque can be found in the table in section 22.1.1.  Then check the wheel bolts/wheel nuts for tightness at regular intervals! 4.2 Registering the Mobile Home CAUTION: Never drive the vehicle without a number plate or insurance cover! Mobile homes are vehicles in the sense of StVZO. Mobile homes must be officially registered before they are driven on public roads. Mobile homes may not be operated without valid insurance.  If the mobile home is fitted with an EU sticker, no further stickers are necessary for driving abroad in Europe, for trips outside Europe a national sticker is also necessary.  If the mobile home is not fitted with an EU sticker, a national sticker is required for all trips abroad. In Germany the national sticker is to be fitted above the right rear light. In other countries the related regulations are to be observed. Contact your nearest KNAUS dealer about the individual formalities required. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 4-1

records.summary: BEFORE THE JOURNEY 4.3 Payload CAUTION:  The maximum total load (see vehicle registration documentation) and the maximum technically permissible axle loads (see section 22.3 Specifications and floor plan with heating diagram) must not be e
records.text: BEFORE THE JOURNEY 4.3 Payload CAUTION:  The maximum total load (see vehicle registration documentation) and the maximum technically permissible axle loads (see section 22.3 Specifications and floor plan with heating diagram) must not be exceeded by the payload!  There is a danger of tyres puncturing if the total admissible weight is exceeded and the tyre pressure is too low. The mobile home could veer out of control!  All additional items carried beyond the information in section 22.2.2.1 Empty weight, reduce the possible payload! In order not to detrimentally affect the handling of your mobile home, take care when loading that the centre of gravity of the payload is directly above the vehicle floor or as close to the vehicle floor as possible. NOTE: The vehicle document gives only the total admissible weight, not the inherent weight of the mobile home. We therefore recommend that you have the vehicle weighed on a public weighbridge before commencing your journey. 4.3.1 Loading the Mobile Home  Ensure that the payload is distributed evenly between the left and right-hand sides of the vehicle.  Secure heavy items (e.g. crockery, cutlery, jars etc.) in low storage areas or on the floor, secured against sliding!  Place lighter objects (e.g. clothes etc.) in the upper storage areas!  When loading the mobile home with a bicycle garage, attention is to be paid to the technically permissible rear axle load! To fasten bicycles, use the KNAUSattachment only!  The bicycle carrier (accessory) may be used only to carry bicycles. The maximum load of the bicycle carrier is: Cycle rack for 2 bicycles (rear mounting) = 50 kg Bicycle carrier PRONTO (for all Cycle rack for 3 bicycles (rear mounting) = 55 kg garage model) for 2 bicycles = 30 kg Cycle rack for 4 bicycles (rear mounting) = 60 kg Bicycle carrier SMV for 4 bicycles = 150 kg  The maximum roof load of the mobile home is 75 kg. records.text: BEFORE THE JOURNEY  Always use the foot mat provided to walk on the roof of the mobile home!  Avoid localised loads (e.g. kneeling) as far as possible if you need to go onto the roof of the mobile home!  It is only allowed to walk on the roof of the mobile home with soft shoes (e.g. sports shoes)! Avoid walking on the roof with textured-soled footwear as any stones embedded in the soles will dent the outer skin of the mobile home!  Take care when climbing onto a wet or icy mobile home roof. There is a danger of slipping or falling off!  The roof bars (optional accessory) may be used to carry only roof loads, e.g. surfboard, rubber dinghies or light canoes!  Always note the increased total height of the mobile home when the roof bars are loaded!  Roof loads must be tied down securely, do not use bungees!  When calculating the payload, sections 22.2.2 to 22.2.4 are to be observed! 4.4 Brakes WARNING: Any defects in the brake system must be immediately repaired by an authorised garage. Ensure that the mobile home’s brake system is operating correctly before commencing any journey. 씰 Test the brakes while driving at moderate speed and ensure that... the vehicle’s brake system is working, the wheels brake evenly, the vehicle does not ‘pull’ to one side. records.title: BEFORE THE JOURNEY 4.5 Tyres
records.summary: BEFORE THE JOURNEY 4.5 Tyres 4.5.1 Safety information concerning the tyres WARNING:  Damaged tyres are a hazard and must be attended to immediately! There is a possibility of the driver losing control of the mobile home if a tyre goes flat
records.text: BEFORE THE JOURNEY 4.5 Tyres 4.5.1 Safety information concerning the tyres WARNING:  Damaged tyres are a hazard and must be attended to immediately! There is a possibility of the driver losing control of the mobile home if a tyre goes flat.  When the mobile home is fully laden, tyres may burst if not inflated to the correct pressure. You may lose control of the vehicle as a result!  Always check tyre pressures with cold tyres.  The minimum statutory depth of tread in the related country must be complied with!  Check tyre pressures (including spare wheel!) before every journey and adjust as necessary. If you cannot avoid driving with low tyre pressure, you should not exceed a maximum speed of 20 km/h.  All 4 tyres on your mobile home should be inflated to the same pressure. The correct tyre pressure is indicated in the tyre pressure table in section 22.1.1 Tyre pressure table.  The profile depth of the tyres is to be checked regularly. The more worn the tread the greater the risk of aquaplaning.  Tyres may deflate in the areas in contact with the ground over long stationary periods when tyre pressures are too low or tyres can gradually deflate. You should therefore inflate the tyres to 0.3 bar above the pressures shown in the table if the unit will be parked for any length of time.  Inadequate tyre pressure can cause tyres to heat up excessively and damage them internally. At high speeds this can cause the tread to separate from the tyre and can even lead to a tyre bursting!  Subsequently correcting the tyre pressure will not cure hidden tyre damage.  Kerbs should only be negotiated slowly and at right angles where possible. Avoid driving over steep and sharp-edged kerbs. Hidden tyre damage can be caused if you drive over kerbs or sharp objects such as stones violently or at too narrow an angle. This damage will have a ‘delayed action’! An accident may be caused by a tyre bursting at high speed!  Regularly check your tyres for damage, e.g. sharp objects sticking in the tyre, holes, cuts, cracks and blisters in the tyre wall. An object lodged in the tyre can also damage the tyre’s interior. Damage should always be examined by a qualified person to see whether it can be repaired. A damaged tyre must be replaced if it cannot be repaired or if a successful repair is in doubt! A damaged tyre can burst!  Never use tyres if you do not know their ‘history’. All tyres age even if they are little used or not used at all. We recommend that you replace the tyres on your mobile home when they are 6 years old - don’t forget the spare wheel! Even the spare wheel should only be used in emergencies after 6 years and driven on with extreme caution! SUN-TRAVELLER 4-4 MJ 2006 • 10.2005 SPORT-TRAVELLER

DURING THE JOURNEY 5.1 Driving Your Mobile Home WARNING:  It is basically permitted to carry persons in the living area of the mobile home during the journey in accordance with StVZO. However these persons may only use the seats designated for this purpose.  Persons sitting in the living area of the mobile home and facing forward, and the driver and front passenger, must wear their 3-point seat belts during the journey!  Persons seated facing the rear in the living area of the mobile home must also wear seat belts if seat belts are fitted!  The mobile home is designed for a maximum speed of 120 km/h. A maximum speed of 130 km/h is shown in the vehicle registration document. The permitted maximum speed for mobile homes in Germany is shown in section 2.4 Safety regulations for participation in traffic. Always drive attentively and with consideration for other road users. The basic mobile home vehicle is classed as a commercial vehicle (small truck). You should therefore drive the mobile home in the same way as you would a light commercial vehicle. CAUTION: When driving into courtyards, tunnels etc. as well as when manoeuvring, it is important that you correctly judge the height, width and length of the mobile home! The dimensions of the mobile home are indicated in the technical data in section 22.3. Follow these useful hints when driving your mobile home:  Never drive faster downhill than you would uphill.  When driving over bridges consider the side-wall and when passing or meeting other vehicles consider that the mobile home can influenced by wind currents. In either situation, you may have to steer farther away from the danger than usual.  Due to the vehicle height you need to be aware of the mobile home’s vulnerability to side winds during the journey.  Do not underestimate the length of your mobile home.  Remember to change gear in good time.  Avoid jerky steering movements. Should the vehicle ever start to skid, take your foot off the brake pedal and gently steer it back into the correct direction of travel. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 5-1

records.summary: LIVING 7. LIVING 7.1 Ventilating the Mobile Home WARNING: The integrated safety ventilation openings (forced ventilation in the roof lights, mushroom vents) must not be obstructed under any circumstances! An increased level of carbon monoxi
records.text: LIVING 7. LIVING 7.1 Ventilating the Mobile Home WARNING: The integrated safety ventilation openings (forced ventilation in the roof lights, mushroom vents) must not be obstructed under any circumstances! An increased level of carbon monoxide (CO) in the air can be fatal!  Providing adequate and correct ventilation for your mobile home is the best way of ensuring optimum conditions of living comfort.  To ensure a continuous flow of air in the mobile home, the forced air vents in the roof, mushroom vents and in the entry must never be covered!  Cooking and wet clothing releases water vapour.  Every person releases up to 35 grams of water into the atmosphere each hour just by breathing. This is why your mobile home must be ventilated with the windows and roof lights depending on the level of humidity. You will find more hints in Chapter 17. Winter Camping. NOTE: Condensation can form under the upholstery during the night. Cushions (expanded foam) should be placed upright and aired to remove any moisture. Condensation may also form inside the acrylic glass double-glazing units in extreme weather conditions. This process is quite normal and can be explained as follows: Acrylic glass - the material from which the windows are made - is an organic material and therefore porous, i.e. moisture and/ or gases can pass through it. With a double acrylic glass panel, extreme weather can change the air conditions in the gap between the two sheets of glass with the result that different conditions bring about a state of equilibrium. Put simply, this means that the air between the two panes tries to match the conditions of the atmosphere surrounding it. If the surrounding atmosphere is continually humid then the space between the two panes of glass also tends to become more humid. This process can be reversed - in dry conditions the air in the gap also tends to become drier. As the temperature rises again the condensation evaporates and the glass demists. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 7-1

Open cover and mosquito blind (normal position)!  Do not tread on the acrylic glass dome!  The glass dome should be closed fully and the blackout blinds opened before commencing your journey and when laying up the mobile home for lengthy periods of time!  Contact your local Service Centre if the roof window develops any problems!  Any snow, ice and other obstructions must be removed before opening the glass dome.  Prior to opening the glass dome under trees, in garages or similar, ensure there is enough clearance! Hints on the cleaning and care of the roof window are given in section 19.4 Care and cleaning of the roof window. The roof window is available as an optional extra and has an electronic control. It makes the interior of the mobile home lighter, provides improved ventilation and gives the living area a pleasant sense of space. There is a cover on the inside of the roof window to act as a curtain and a mosquito blind. The cover and mosquito blind can be used separately or together. The bad weather position enables the glass dome to be opened approx. 15 mm in the rain so that no water can enter the interior, and the wind cannot open the glass dome. records.text: SLEEPING 8. SLEEPING 8.1 Converting the seating modules for sleeping The alcove bed, tail section bed and the bunk beds are available for use at any time. The seating modules can also be converted to beds in just a few simple operations. WARNING:  Before using the alcove bed the guard (safety net) must be pulled up and attached to the fixtures provided.  Before the alcove bed is used by children you should also ensure that the children cannot slip through either side of the safety net and possibly fall to the floor.  Bunk beds must be made safe with the guards provided prior to use.  Before bunk beds are used by children you should also ensure that the children cannot slip through beneath the guard or get over the guard and possibly fall to the floor. 8.1.1 Converting the Seating Module with Height-Adjustable Table to a Bed 1. Release the table by moving the handle in the direction shown by the arrow, and lower the table as far as it will go. The table feet will move like a parallelogram. 2. Pull the side seat cushions into the centre. Place the back cushions into the spaces. When raised, the table will automatically engage in its initial position. Converting the Height-Adjustable Table to a Bed SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 8-1

records.summary: GAS SUPPLY 9. GAS SUPPLY 9.1 General Notes on the Gas Supply NOTE: The overall gas system is designed for an operating pressure of 30 millibar [mbar]! WARNING: 墌 Repairs and modifications to the gas system may only be carried out by the aut
records.text: GAS SUPPLY 9. GAS SUPPLY 9.1 General Notes on the Gas Supply NOTE: The overall gas system is designed for an operating pressure of 30 millibar [mbar]! WARNING: 墌 Repairs and modifications to the gas system may only be carried out by the authorised service centre! 墌 It is essential to follow the safety instructions and safety information when using the gas system or gas appliances! 墌 Altering the gas system or appliances yourself is prohibited and dangerous! 墌 The customer may only connect the pressure regulator to the gas bottle. All other work must be carried out by an authorised service centre. 墌 Never search for gas leaks with a cigarette lighter or other naked flames! 墌 The entire gas system has been designed according to the applicable regulations governing LPG appliances and fires in mobile homes, and has been tested and certified by an engineer. 墌 All fitted gas-fired appliances are ignition-protected, so if the flame goes out then the ignition safety system isolates the gas supply automatically. Despite this safety device you should always turn off the appropriate gas tap when any of the appliances are not in use. 墌 Should a fault ever occur, (e.g. gas consumption is excessive or you smell gas) follow the safety information and have the fault repaired by a service centre. 墌 Get the service centre to certify the repair or modification to the gas system in the gas test certificate (yellow test certificate) and always insist on a gas leak test being carried out. 墌 To ensure a continuous flow of air in the mobile home, the forced air vents in the roof, mushroom vents and in the entry must never be covered! SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 9-1

records.summary: GAS SUPPLY NOTE: The gas system should be checked every 2 years by a gas engineer. The vehicle keeper is responsible for testing the gas system! 9.2 LPG The gas-fired appliances can be operated with propane or butane or a mixture of these t
records.text: GAS SUPPLY NOTE: The gas system should be checked every 2 years by a gas engineer. The vehicle keeper is responsible for testing the gas system! 9.2 LPG The gas-fired appliances can be operated with propane or butane or a mixture of these two LPG types. Retail stockists usually supply the gas in 5 kg or 11 kg refillable or returnable bottles. These bottles must be kept in the gas locker. The gas locker should be kept secure from unauthorised access at all times! NOTE: You should use pure propane for winter camping as butane will not gasify below freezing point. 9.3 Placing Gas Bottles in the Gas Locker CAUTION: The gas locker flap can be opened and shut by pressing lightly! 씰 Place the gas bottles upright in the gas locker and secure them firmly with the straps provided. Fit the pressure regulator to the gas bottle by hand (never use spanners, pliers etc.). 9.4 General Information on the Gas Consumption The amount of gas you use will depend on how much you use the gas appliances:  The Trumatic (heater and hot water boiler) consumes between 170 and 500 g/h depending on the weather and the interior temperature setting (heater) and amount of use (hot water boiler)  The refrigerator consumes about 18 g/h  The refrigerator consumes about 300 g/h SUN-TRAVELLER 9-2 MJ 2006 • 10.2005 SPORT-TRAVELLER

records.title: GAS SUPPLY 9.7 Changing the Gas Bottle
records.summary: GAS SUPPLY 9.7 Changing the Gas Bottle WARNING:  The customer may only connect the pressure regulator to the gas bottle. All other work must be carried out by an authorised service centre.  Never use a lighted or other open source of ligh
records.text: GAS SUPPLY 9.7 Changing the Gas Bottle WARNING:  The customer may only connect the pressure regulator to the gas bottle. All other work must be carried out by an authorised service centre.  Never use a lighted or other open source of light when changing the gas bottle!  There is still some gas left even in an “empty” gas bottle. For this reason exercise extreme caution when changing the gas bottle!  After changing the gas bottle, it is to be checked whether there are any leaks! CAUTION:  The gas regulator is only to be fitted and removed by hand. Do not use any tools for this purpose!  When changing the gas bottle, it is to be ensured that the gas hose is in good condition and is laid without any kinks! 1. Close gas bottle stop valve (1). 2. Unscrew gas regulator (2) from the gas bottle by hand (caution: left-hand thread). 1 3. Undo fastening strap (3) and remove empty gas bottle from the gas locker. 4. Place empty gas bottle in a suitable place, never leave empty gas bottles unsecured in the gas locker. 2 5. Place full gas bottle in the mounting in the gas locker and secure with fastening strap. 6. Screw gas regulator onto the gas bottle by hand (caution: left- hand thread). 3 7. Open gas bottle stop valve (1). Changing the Gas Bottle SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 9-5

records.summary: GAS SUPPLY NOTE:  If the pressure in the bottle being used sinks to under 5 bar, the valve will switch over automatically and gas will be taken from the spare bottle.  In extremely cold weather as well as high gas consumption, the bottle
records.text: GAS SUPPLY NOTE:  If the pressure in the bottle being used sinks to under 5 bar, the valve will switch over automatically and gas will be taken from the spare bottle.  In extremely cold weather as well as high gas consumption, the bottle pressure can fall to under 5 bar although there is still gas in the bottle. The bottle defined for use by the rotary knob is always emptied first. The gas pressure regulator set then automatically switches to the previously defined reserve bottle. When the remote display is switched on, the related indicator A (item 5, page 9-8) or B (item 6, page 9-8) goes out and indicates an empty gas bottle. 9.8.3 Important notes on the use of the DuoComfort  The gas bottle must always be in a vertical position and secured against falling!  The high-pressure hose fittings are suitable for standard 3 kg, 5 kg, 11 kg and 33 kg gas bottles.  The high-pressure hoses are to be installed so that the pressure gauge points upward (see image page 9-6).  Do not kink or tightly bend high-pressure hoses! 9.8.4 Changing the gas bottle on the DuoComfort WARNING: When changing the gas bottles, you must be aware that there is still gas in an “empty” gas bottle. For this reason smoking and any form of naked flame are forbidden! The Truma-DuoComfort enables an empty gas bottle to be changed without interrupting the operation of the appliances, as all the appliance continue to be supplied from the reserve bottle. 1. Close the valve on the empty gas bottle. 2. Unscrew the high-pressure hose from the gas bottle and remove the gas bottle. 3. Set up the full gas bottle, secure it with the fastening strap and screw the high-pressure hose to the gas bottle. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 9-7

records.text: WATER SUPPLY 10. WATER SUPPLY 10.1 Fresh Water Supply CAUTION: To prevent the water pump from seizing, do not operate it without water! All Sun-Traveller models have a fresh water tank with a capacity of 106 litres and a water pump (immersion pump) that is supplied by the 12 V electrical system. All Sport-Traveller models have a fresh water tank with a capacity of 115 litres and a water pump (immersion pump) that is supplied by the 12 V electrical system. The fresh water tank is fitted in the double floor on both models. The fresh water tank is encased in an insulating shell that is heated by a heating spur from the heater. This keeps the fresh water tank frost-proof even in low temperatures. The heating for the fresh water tank is described in section 10.7. The water pump is located in the fresh water tank and is placed in operation when water is drawn from the taps. 10.2 Checking the fill level in the fresh water and waster water tanks 1. Press the button (2) on the on-board control. 2. The fill level indicator (4) shows the current fill level. 2 To check the fill level in the waste water tank, proceed as follows: 1. Press the button (3) on the on-board control. Check 2. records.title: WATER SUPPLY 10.3 Wastewater Disposal
records.summary: WATER SUPPLY 10.3 Wastewater Disposal NOTE: The wastewater tank should only be drained on sites with suitable sewage systems or specially designated disposal facilities! Waster water is collected in a 100 litre waster water tank in all Sun-
records.text: WATER SUPPLY 10.3 Wastewater Disposal NOTE: The wastewater tank should only be drained on sites with suitable sewage systems or specially designated disposal facilities! Waster water is collected in a 100 litre waster water tank in all Sun-Traveller models and in a 105 litre tank in all Sport- Traveller models. The wastewater tank is mounted under the floor and can be encased in an insulating shell that is heated by a heating spur as an option. This keeps the wastewater tank frost-proof even in low temperatures. The heating for the waster water tank is described in section 10.7. The wastewater is drained using the drain valve (ball valve) fitted to the wastewater tank. A drainage hose (optional extra) can also be attached to the drainage valve to run the waste to special disposal sites. In modern camping sites, the drainage hose is used for connecting the waste tank and the sewer line of the camping site. 10.4 Emptying the water system The complete water system should be drained fully if it is not to be used for a time, especially before the mobile home is laid up for the winter. NOTE: We recommend that you change the water in the fresh water tank regularly (e.g. weekly) even when the tank is full, as bacteria form in the fresh water after just a few days and will give the water an unpleasant taste. 1. Drain fresh water tank as per section 10.5. 2. Drain wastewater tank as per section 10.6. 3. Drain the hot water heater according to section 12.1.7 (Truma) or 12.3.2 (Alde). records.title: WATER SUPPLY 10.5 Emptying the Fresh Water Tank
records.summary: WATER SUPPLY 10.5 Emptying the Fresh Water Tank 1. Switch off the water pump using the rocker switch (item 11, page 10-1) on the on-board control. 2. Open all water taps in the mobile home. 3. Remove the cleaning cover in the fresh water ta
records.text: WATER SUPPLY 10.5 Emptying the Fresh Water Tank 1. Switch off the water pump using the rocker switch (item 11, page 10-1) on the on-board control. 2. Open all water taps in the mobile home. 3. Remove the cleaning cover in the fresh water tank. 4. Remove the plugs from the base of the tank. 5. Allow the fresh water tank to drain fully. 6. Check the fill level using the fill level indicator (item 4, page 10-1) and button (item 2, page 10-1) on the on-board control. 7. Push the plug back into the drain hole and replace the cleaning cover. 10.6 Emptying the Wastewater Tank The drainage valve for the waste tank is located outside the mobile home on the underbody. NOTE: The wastewater tank should only be drained on sites with suitable sewage systems or specially designated disposal facilities! 1. Move the drain valve to the „OPEN“ position and drain wastewater at a suitable disposal facility. 2. Check the fill level using the fill level indicator (item 4, page 10-1) and button (item 3, page 10-1) on the on-board control. 3. Turn the valve handle to „CLOSE“. When the drain valve (ball valve) is closed a small amount of residual water escapes from the valve through a channel used as a frost drain. This prevents the ball valve from freezing up. 10.7 Heating the fresh water and waste water tanks  When the fresh water tank or the waster water tank is full, the spur valve must be open for heating the tank. 씰 To prevent freezing or overheating, the heat to the tanks can be increased or decreased by regulating the warm air spur valve (actuating the rotary knob or the cord).
