records.title: POWER SUPPLY 11.3 On-board control
records.summary: POWER SUPPLY 11.3 On-board control The on-board control can be used to turn on and off the electrical 12-Volt appliances „water pump“ and „appliance circuits 1 and 2“ either separately with their respective rocker switches or together with
records.text: POWER SUPPLY 11.3 On-board control The on-board control can be used to turn on and off the electrical 12-Volt appliances „water pump“ and „appliance circuits 1 and 2“ either separately with their respective rocker switches or together with the 12-Volt system main switch. The ceiling lighting can be switched on and off with the respective direct switch in the on-board control and the switch beside the entry door. All electrical appliances are each protected with fuses. The fuses are located in the distributor box under the left-hand seating module. The fuse for the refrigerator in 12 Volt operation is located in the distributor box. The power circuit for the water pump has a 10 A fuse in the distributor box. The power circuit for the direct light switches the circuit on and off for the direct light. The power circuits for appliances 1 and 2 are each equipped with a 15 A fuse located in the distributor box. The on-board control is equipped with low-charge protection (battery monitor). The battery monitor monitors power circuits 1 and 2 and the water pump circuit and protects the auxiliary battery from damaging low discharging. If the auxiliary battery voltage falls under 10.8 V, all the appliances that can be switched on and off with the main switch are turned off. This situation is the indicated by the red indicator lamp lighting up. These appliances can be turned on again for about 2 minutes by pressing the illuminated button, they will then be turned off again automatically. The starter battery voltage (battery 1) and the auxiliary battery voltage (battery 2) can be queried with buttons. The voltage status is then shown in the display field by means of a 10 position, multi-coloured series of LEDs: Display field 1 to 2 red Battery must be charged Display field 3 to 4 yellow Battery is almost flat Display field 5 to 10 green Battery is charged sufficiently The LEDs in battery symbol 1 (auxiliary batter) are always illuminated if the auxiliary battery is being charged in mains- or driving-operation. The LED in battery symbol 1 (starter battery) is illuminated if the starter battery is being charged, i.e. if either the motor is running or batteries 1 and 2 are running in parallel. The current fill levels for fresh water and waster water can be called up with buttons. The fill level is then shown in the display field by means of a 10 position, multi-coloured series of LEDs: Display field 1 to 3 Tank 1/4 full Display field 1 to 5 Tank 1/2 full Display field 1 to 7 Tank 3/4 full Display field 1 to 10 Tank 1/1 full You will find further information about the on-board control in the separate operating instructions from the manufacturer. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 11-3

records.text: POWER SUPPLY 11.6 12 V supply from backup battery and charger 11.6.1 Backup Battery WARNING:  No maintenance work is to be performed on the maintenance- free gel battery! The battery would be destroyed and there is a danger of the battery exploding.  The Gel battery may only be replaced with another Gel battery! The auxiliary battery (battery 2) can be accessed through the service flap. The main battery switch and the charger are located under the left-hand seating module. This means that the mobile homes have their own 12 Volt power supply. The charge of the starter battery (battery 1) and the backup battery (battery 2) can be checked by pressing the corresponding button (item 6 or 7, page 11-4) on the LED array (item 5, page 11-4) on the on-board control. It is advisable to charge up the auxiliary battery with the charger for at least 18 hours before use. This requires switching the main switch on (item 1, page 11-4). Switch off all electrical appliances while charging so as to achieve a rapid and optimum charge. Charging should be supervised. This is done with the button (item 7, page 11-4) and the LED display (item 5, page 11-4) on the on-board control. Before connecting up to the 230 V mains you should check the level of charge in the auxiliary battery by pressing the button on the LED array. Once you have connected up to the 230-Volt supply, press the button again and watch the LED display. The LED display should now light up in the green area toward „1/1“. If it does, this indicates that the charger is working correctly. If the LED display does not change, this indicates that the charger is not charging. You should try and identify the cause, i.e. check the 2 A, 2.5 A and 50 A fuses behind the backup battery under the seating module. If you are unable to find the cause, contact an appointed dealer. CAUTION: A battery that is left flat for more than 3 weeks is damaged beyond repair and must be replaced. A flat battery must be charged up with the charger for at least 48 hours before use provided the battery was not flat for more than 3 weeks. SUN-TRAVELLER 11-6 MJ 2006 • 10.2005 SPORT-TRAVELLER

records.title: POWER SUPPLY NOTE:
records.summary: POWER SUPPLY NOTE: The auxiliary battery is still under a load of approximately 20 to 65 mA from electrical consumers (heating, charger, on-board control, etc.) even after switching the appliances off. Therefore, the charge status of the au
records.text: POWER SUPPLY NOTE: The auxiliary battery is still under a load of approximately 20 to 65 mA from electrical consumers (heating, charger, on-board control, etc.) even after switching the appliances off. Therefore, the charge status of the auxiliary battery is to be checked regularly to prevent any damage to it! CAUTION: The hot water boiler drains automatically when the battery monitor shuts the power off. The heater is protected by a battery monitor to prevent it from fully discharging the auxiliary battery. If the main switch (item 1 page 11-4) on the on-board control is switched on, the battery monitor will switch off the heater when the battery voltage drops to approx. 11.0 V. If the main switch is shut off, the heating is switched off when a voltage of approx. 12.4 Volts. NOTE: The hot water boiler will drain each time the battery monitor turns off the heater. CAUTION:  The auxiliary batters is to be fully charged and then switched off with the main switch for longer periods of storage (item 1, page 9-11).  The fully charged battery should be disconnected and removed from the vehicle in winter.  A complete discharge can damage the battery beyond repair.  The backup battery may only be charged with a suitable charger when off the vehicle. The entire 12-Volt system can be switched on and off with the main switch on the on-board control (item 1, page 11-4). If the rocker switch is in position » «, then the 12 Volt system is switched off. However the electrical supply to the refrigerator (WAECO) when in 12 V operation, the ceiling light and the heater remains on. SUN-TRAVELLER SPORT-TRAVELLER MJ 2006 • 10.2005 11-7
